note: M26 A: the Book of Laws. Five chapters, each with two rival paths of three tiers. A path's tier 2 needs its tier 1 signed, tier 3 its tier 2. Signing tier 1 of a path locks the rival path; repealing a path from the top down reopens it. inkDays: no law can be signed for this long after any law is signed or repealed. lawCooldown: a law signed or repealed cannot be changed again for this long. enactDays: a signed law takes this long to take hold. Each law: headline (one line, what the player will feel), blurb, cost (coin), authority (needed to sign), effects (summed into the realm's law effects as they take hold), opinion (where groups settle while it stands), meters (moved at once on signing: love, fear, unrest), reaction (one line from the people and the court), repeal (moved at once on repealing; groups who liked it sour by repealShock of their liking), unlocks (an act of the crown), choose (a choice made on signing).

laws.name: Assizes
laws.headline: Unrest in every town and city falls by 8, and Love rises month by month.
laws.blurb: Travelling judges ride the circuits and hear the commons' grievances in the king's name.
laws.reaction: The commons crowd the first assize at Vizima; the lords mutter about royal judges in their halls.

laws.name: Royal pardons
laws.headline: Unlocks Pardon: a town's Unrest falls by 15 (every 60 days).
laws.blurb: The king's mercy can be granted to a whole town's petty offenders at once.
laws.reaction: Mothers bless the king's name at the prison gates; the sheriffs complain they will be catching the same thieves twice.

laws.name: Charter of the commons
laws.headline: Unrest caused by taxes is halved.
laws.blurb: The crown swears to tax by custom and consent, and the towns believe it.
laws.reaction: The charter is read in every market square; the barons call it a surrender.

laws.name: Curfews and the watch
laws.headline: Unrest falls by 10 everywhere, Fear grows each month, and foreign agents are caught more often.
laws.blurb: Bells at dusk, the watch on every corner, and the stocks for anyone abroad after dark.
laws.reaction: The streets empty at the curfew bell; the taverns curse the watch under their breath.

laws.name: Public executions
laws.headline: Unlocks Hang the ringleaders: a town's Unrest falls by 20, Fear rises by 15 (every 30 days).
laws.blurb: Justice done where all can see it.
laws.reaction: A scaffold rises in Vizima's square. Nobody laughs at the watch any more.

laws.name: The king's riders
laws.headline: Bandit threats near the roads are halved, foreign agents are caught more often, and Fear grows.
laws.blurb: Armed riders in the king's colours patrol every high road and hang highwaymen where they catch them.
laws.reaction: Bodies swing at the crossroads and the merchants travel without guards again.

laws.name: Open markets
laws.headline: Market dues in the towns rise by 30%.
laws.blurb: Tolls between the crown's towns are struck down and any honest trader may sell in any market.
laws.reaction: Carts queue at the open gates; the toll-keepers look for other work.

laws.name: Merchant charters
laws.headline: Partners abroad pay 25% more for our goods.
laws.blurb: Royal charters to the great merchant houses carry the crown's name into every foreign market.
laws.reaction: The merchant houses hang the royal arms over their doors and raise their prices abroad.

laws.name: The royal bank
laws.headline: Loans cost half the interest, and the crown can borrow 10,000 more.
laws.blurb: The crown keeps its own counting house, and the Vivaldis lend more cheaply to a king with his own bank.
laws.reaction: The new counting house opens on the square; the old moneylenders shut their shutters.

laws.name: Guild monopolies
laws.headline: The crafts earn 30% more for the crown.
laws.blurb: Each craft is granted to one chartered guild, which pays the crown well for the privilege.
laws.reaction: The guildmasters toast the king; the free craftsmen burn their tools in protest.

laws.name: Royal mines
laws.headline: Gold and silver mines yield 50% more.
laws.blurb: Every seam belongs to the crown, worked by the crown's own overseers.
laws.reaction: The king's assayers move into the mine towns; the lords who held the seams are not consoled.

laws.name: Royal granaries
laws.headline: Grain stores hold 50% more, and unlocks Open the granaries: end hunger in a town (every 60 days).
laws.blurb: Great stone granaries in every town, filled at harvest by the king's factors.
laws.reaction: The granaries fill under guard; the poor know where the bread will come from in a hard winter.

laws.name: Seasonal conscription
laws.headline: Every muster brings 50% more men.
laws.blurb: Every able man owes the crown a season's service when the levy is called.
laws.reaction: The muster rolls are read in every village; the young men look to the woods.

laws.name: Militia drills
laws.headline: Levy companies fight a grade better.
laws.blurb: Sunday drill on the green: spear, shield and keeping the line.
laws.reaction: The village greens ring with drill; the alehouses empty on Sundays.

laws.name: Every man a soldier
laws.headline: Musters bring twice the men, but the works lose a tenth of their output while levies are raised.
laws.blurb: Every household keeps a spear by the door and answers when the crown calls.
laws.reaction: Spears hang over every hearth; the fields will want for hands when the drums beat.

laws.name: Standing companies
laws.headline: Companies cost a quarter less to keep.
laws.blurb: Long contracts, regular pay and barracks of their own make soldiers cheaper by the year.
laws.reaction: The companies sign on for years; the lords grumble that the king no longer needs their men.

laws.name: The military academy
laws.headline: Companies gain experience twice as fast.
laws.blurb: Old captains teach the young ones what the last war cost.
laws.reaction: The academy opens at Vizima; second sons of the lesser houses queue at its gate.

laws.name: Royal knights
laws.headline: Knights cost half as much, and every army marches 10 points bolder.
laws.blurb: An order of knights sworn to the crown alone.
laws.reaction: The new order rides through Vizima in the king's colours; the barons count their own knights and frown.

laws.name: Poor relief
laws.headline: Half as many die of hunger, and Love grows.
laws.blurb: Bread and soup at the temple doors, paid for by the crown.
laws.reaction: Bread lines form at the temple doors, and the priestesses pray for the king.

laws.name: Hospices
laws.headline: Half as many die of plague.
laws.blurb: Houses of healing in every town, tended by Melitele's sisters at the crown's cost.
laws.reaction: Melitele's sisters open the hospices; the sick are carried in from the villages.

laws.name: Royal feasts
laws.headline: Unlocks Hold a feast: Love +10 across the realm (every 90 days).
laws.blurb: The crown keeps open table on the great days of the year.
laws.reaction: The court plans its first open table; the cooks of Vizima hire every hand in the city.

laws.name: Long hours
laws.headline: Every works turns out 30% more, and Unrest rises by 5.
laws.blurb: Dawn to dusk, and by lamplight in winter.
laws.reaction: The workshop bells ring an hour earlier; the workers ring them back with curses.

laws.name: Debtors' labour
laws.headline: Twice as many repair crews from the same hands.
laws.blurb: Debtors work off what they owe on the crown's walls and works.
laws.reaction: Chained debtors haul stone on the walls; the moneylenders approve.

laws.name: Prison gangs
laws.headline: Repairs go twice as fast, and Fear grows.
laws.blurb: Every prisoner in the realm labours on the crown's works under the lash.
laws.reaction: Gangs in irons rebuild the broken works; mothers keep their sons indoors.

laws.name: Freedom of worship
laws.headline: Clashes between the faiths are halved.
laws.blurb: Every faith may keep its shrines and its feasts under the king's peace.
laws.reaction: The druids walk openly into Vizima; the Fire's priests preach against the king's softness.

laws.name: The non-human charter
laws.headline: Crafts earn a quarter more wherever non-humans are a tenth of the people or more, and non-humans settle.
laws.blurb: Dwarves, elves and halflings are the king's subjects with the same rights as any.
laws.reaction: The dwarves of Vizima raise a toast to the charter; the Fire's zealots tear it from the church doors.

laws.name: Licensed mages
laws.headline: Unlocks Summon the court mage: end a monster threat or a plague in one place (every 120 days).
laws.blurb: Mages may practise under royal licence, and the crown keeps one at court.
laws.reaction: A sorceress takes rooms in the palace; the Hierarch declares a day of prayer against her.

laws.name: Faith of the crown
laws.headline: The chosen faith's Devotion grows twice as fast, and its faithful rejoice.
laws.blurb: The crown takes one faith for its own and endows it.
laws.reaction: The king hears mass in the chosen faith; the other temples count their faithful.

laws.name: Restrictions on non-humans
laws.headline: Fear grows, the Eternal Fire rejoices, and non-humans grow restless and leave.
laws.blurb: Non-humans may not own land, bear arms or live outside their quarters.
laws.reaction: Walls go up round the non-human quarters; the Fire's preachers call it the first step.

laws.name: The inquisition
laws.headline: Unlocks Witch hunt: clear the Scoia'tael from a region (every 60 days). Foreign agents are caught far more often, and Fear grows.
laws.blurb: The Fire's inquisitors may question anyone, anywhere, in the king's name.
laws.reaction: Grey-robed inquisitors ride out of Vizima; the forests go very quiet.
